subject: Order form: commit tranche, billing entity flow & VAT evidence needed
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Emma Thomas <emma.thomas@nexelhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form: commit tranche, billing entity flow & VAT evidence needed

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Attached is our latest Order Form redline (Nexel_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf) and a short pricing appendix (pricing_commit_tranche.xlsx) that shows the commit broken into a 40% signature tranche and a 60% activation tranche tied to two milestone events. Quick summary of the commercial points we redlined:

- Commit phasing: 40% on signature, 30% on stage-1 activation (pilot completion), 30% on full production activation.
- Invoicing cadence: Redwood invoices per milestone; each invoice payable per the net terms below.
- Net terms: Redwood standard Net 30; we noted Nexus procurement prefers Net 45 — open to discuss but need finance sign-off.
- Billing entity / tax: We proposed Redwood EU (DE) as invoice entity for EU customers. To apply reverse-charge (no VAT collected), we need Nexel Health's EU VAT ID on file; if not provided, the Order Form conservatively preserves Redwood's right to gross-up or withhold local taxes as required.

Can your procurement team confirm which legal entity will accept invoices (Nexel Health GmbH vs Nexel Health UK Ltd) and whether you can provide a VAT certificate? If Nexel needs Net 45 we can escalate to Finance but want to avoid delaying signature.

Requesting internal legal and finance review (Kimberly + Jonas) on the redline tax language below — if we can agree to the reverse-charge approach contingent on VAT proof, we can keep the Order Form tight and move to e-signature.

Requested calendar: please confirm by end-of-day Wednesday (26 Mar) if procurement can supply VAT proof and entity for invoicing. If not, we will propose an alternate gross-up wording.

Attachments: Nexel_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf; pricing_commit_tranche.xlsx

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

---
Note: pricing spreadsheet shows proposed milestone triggers and token estimates for each tranche.
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Mar 2025 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order form: commit tranche, billing entity flow & VAT evidence needed

Lauren —

Thanks for the context and the redline. I reviewed the tax/billing language and have two recommendations to keep the deal moving while protecting Redwood:

1) Reverse-charge clause: replace the catch-all with a conditional statement — we will not collect VAT if Nexel provides a valid EU VAT registration number and a signed certificate within 5 business days of signature. If they don’t provide it, invoices will include VAT at the applicable rate and Nexel is responsible for the tax (no later claims).

2) Gross-up vs withholding: do not include a blanket gross-up for Redwood. Instead, add a fallback: if local law requires withholding, the customer shall either (a) provide tax receipts and pay the grossed-up amount, or (b) provide proof of tax paid and Redwood will credit appropriately. This avoids unilateral gross-up claims.

Operational asks for Finance (Jonas): confirm acceptance of Net 45 for this account. If Finance requires Net 30, we should offer a limited exception with a 2% fee for Net 45 or require a PO upfront for the signature tranche.

I’ll prepare a one-page legal summary of the suggested edits (legal_comment_summary.docx) that we can share with Nexel so procurement can accept language without heavy redlines.

I’m copying Ben to coordinate the customer communication.

—Kimberly Park
Lead Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

---
(Internal only) Proposed redline snippet to share with customer: “Customer shall provide a valid VAT number and a VAT evidence document within five (5) business days of signature. Absent such evidence, Redwood may apply VAT to invoices. Any tax withholding required by applicable law shall be the responsibility of Customer unless Customer provides official tax receipts within thirty (30) days after payment, in which case Redwood will issue a credit for amounts demonstrably paid to the local tax authority.”
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Thomas <emma.thomas@nexelhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@nexelhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Mar 2025 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order form: commit tranche, billing entity flow & VAT evidence needed

Hi Emma / Nexel procurement team —

Appreciate the quick discussion last week. Following our internal review (copied Kim and Lauren), we propose the following practical approach to unblock signature today:

- Commercial: 40% due on signature, remaining 60% split across two activation milestones as shown in the attached pricing_commit_tranche.xlsx.
- Billing entity: Redwood can invoice Nexel Health GmbH (EU) if you confirm the EU entity and provide the VAT certificate. If Nexel prefers invoices to go to the UK entity, please confirm PO and VAT treatment.
- Net terms: Redwood standard Net 30; given internal constraints we can sign Net 45 for this customer as a one-off if procurement provides an upfront PO covering the 40% signature tranche.
- Tax fallback: as Kim suggested, please provide VAT evidence within five business days of signature. If we do not receive it, invoices will include VAT at the local rate.

To move quickly, I’ve attached a customer-facing summary we can send to procurement. If procurement can provide the VAT PDF and entity name now, I’ll push the Order Form to DocuSign and route the first invoice immediately upon signature.

Link to DocuSign (draft): https://app.docusign.com/sign/ABC12345

Thanks — I’ll stand by for the VAT file and PO number.

Best regards,

Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0122

Attachment: pricing_commit_tranche.xlsx
From: Emma Thomas <emma.thomas@nexelhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nexelhealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Mar 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order form: commit tranche, billing entity flow & VAT evidence needed

Ben / Lauren —

Thanks — procurement reviewed internally. We can confirm Nexel Health GmbH will accept invoices from Redwood EU (DE). I’ve attached our EU VAT certificate (Nexel_VAT.pdf) and raised a PO for the 40% signature tranche (PO# NX-2025-3342). Procurement requests Net 45 as a firm term; they are not able to provide an upfront prepayment beyond the PO.

Given the PO, can Redwood confirm acceptance of Net 45 and proceed to send the final Order Form to DocuSign? If you need the formal tax certificate signed, let me know; otherwise the attached PDF should be sufficient for your records.

Happy to hop on a 15-min call if there are any last open items.

—Emma Thomas
Head of Procurement | Nexel Health
emma.thomas@nexelhealth.com

Attachment referenced: Nexel_VAT.pdf
